# Retrieval eval

`tests/retrieval_eval.rs` runs the code behind `scriptorium bench` on the
vault in `vault/` and compares every case's rank with `baseline.json`. The
`retrieval-eval` workflow runs it on pull requests that touch search,
embedding, vault or bench code.

## What it measures

`vault/` holds 33 invented pages about a research institute: projects,
people, sites, instruments, vendors and events, joined by wikilinks. Every
name in it is made up. `vault/.scriptorium/benchmarks.json` holds 46 cases.
Each description is `<id> <kind> <lang>`:

| Kind | Cases | The answer is on |
|---|---|---|
| `single` | 14 | the page the question names |
| `hop1` | 14 | a page one wikilink away from it |
| `hop2` | 12 | a page two wikilinks away from it |
| `keyword` | 6 | the page that holds all the query's words |

40 cases are in English and 6 in Ukrainian. A case's rank is the position
of its first expected page among the distinct pages retrieved, and a page
past rank 5 is a miss. The test prints hit@1, hit@5 and MRR@5 for every
kind and language.

The question cases contain punctuation, and FTS5 `MATCH` rejects most of
them, so they test vector and graph retrieval. The `keyword` cases are
plain words that `MATCH` accepts. The test also runs them through hybrid
search with only the keyword list on, and checks that it finds their
expected page.

## Frozen embeddings

`vectors.f32` holds a 768-d little-endian f32 vector for each text in
`vectors.json`, in the same order: every chunk the reindex embeds and every
case query. They come from EmbeddingGemma 2
(`embeddinggemma-2:270m-q8_0-text`, Ollama 0.40.10, recorded 2026-10-28).
The run needs no model and no network, and gives the same ranks every time.
A text with no frozen vector fails the test, and so does a `vectors.json`
or `baseline.json` recorded for another model.

## Commands

Run the eval:

```bash
cargo test -p scriptorium-core --test retrieval_eval -- --nocapture
```

After an intended ranking change, rewrite the baseline and commit it with
the change, so the diff shows which cases moved:

```bash
SCRIPTORIUM_EVAL_UPDATE=1 cargo test -p scriptorium-core --test retrieval_eval -- --nocapture
```

After editing `vault/` or the cases, or after a chunking change, record new
vectors. This needs Ollama 0.40.4 or later with the model pulled
(`ollama pull embeddinggemma-2:270m-q8_0-text`):

```bash
SCRIPTORIUM_EVAL_RECORD=1 SCRIPTORIUM_EVAL_UPDATE=1 cargo test -p scriptorium-core --test retrieval_eval -- --nocapture
```

`SCRIPTORIUM_EVAL_REPORT=<path>` also writes every case's ranked pages.

## Generated files

`vectors.f32`, `vectors.json` and `baseline.json` are generated by the
commands above. Review the `baseline.json` diff; skip the vector files.

## Limits

The pages and labels are synthetic and written by one author, and the
questions paraphrase the pages, so the set is easier than real use. Only
one embedding model is frozen, and query expansion stays off, as in
`scriptorium bench`.
